A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same grouped scaling-law discovery research and expression/optimizer co-evolution framework, despite renaming and substantial expansion. Text, equations, figures and tables support comparison. v2's Appendices A-D were included; v1 contains no appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4.2-4.3 report original discovery experiments across five scenarios, an optimizer ablation and MoE fitting analyses using previously published experimental data.

after.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original seven-task agent evaluations, downstream application results, ablations, iteration analyses and two human-expert law-fitting outcomes.

M1.justification: EvoSLD becomes SLDAgent while retaining the core procedure: jointly evolve expression and fitting code, fit coefficients by control group, and select the best candidate. v2 adds a downstream inference procedure that analytically minimizes a discovered loss surface to produce learning-rate and batch-size recommendations (Sections 4.4 and B.5). Expanded search implementation descriptions alone do not establish a new discovery algorithm.

E1.justification: All five earlier scenarios remain. v2 adds inference-parallelism scaling and learning-rate/batch-size loss prediction, expanding coverage to seven tasks. It also evaluates downstream hyperparameter optimization and model selection on FLAN, Wikitext and Gigaword (Sections 2 and 4.4-4.5).

E2.justification: The Naive SLD, PySR and GPlearn comparisons disappear. v2 introduces seven coding-agent comparators, including Aider, OpenHands and Codex, plus provider-specific CLI comparisons (Tables 2-3). Human laws remain, and the fixed-optimizer ablation survives as SLDAgent-law-only in Table 10. Table 4 adds five model-selection comparators.

E3.justification: The vocabulary, MoE and data-constrained tasks change from random 80/20 splits to scale-based holdouts; SFT and domain-mixture split designs are retained. v2 introduces primary R2 reporting with clipped task averages, changes NMSE normalization from combined-data to test-data variance, and changes NMAE normalization to absolute target magnitude. Reported search settings change from three to five islands and migration every 20 to 25 generations. New application protocols include model selection using 6.25% of the data.

E4.justification: The fixed-BFGS ablation is retained and evaluated in the revised seven-task setting (Appendix B.7). v2 adds evolutionary-iteration trajectories for three difficulty levels (Figure 4). It removes v1's six-panel MoE comparison across seeds and baselines, together with the numerical verification of fitted human-law coefficients (v1 Figure 2 and Table 3).

E5.justification: v1 reports three-run means and individual MoE seed examples. v2 retains three-run averaging, specifies successful runs for Tables 5-6, and newly reports NMSE, NMAE and R2 standard deviations for four SLDAgent backbones across all seven tasks (Tables 7-9). Figure 4 also displays ten runs for the new iteration analysis; this does not establish increased runs for the main comparisons.

E6.justification: The five-scenario results are replaced and expanded under revised settings; v2 Table 3 reports average R2 of 0.913 for SLDAgent with GPT-5 and 0.738 for Human. Exact SFT-law rediscovery in v1 becomes a different shifted-power law in v2. New application findings include validation loss 2.0776 versus a grid optimum of 2.0762, and 100% relative accuracy on all three model-selection datasets. Changed splits and normalizations prevent interpreting these as matched-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: The grouped-law formulation is retained in simplified form. v2 adds localized mathematical derivations: a quadratic log-loss optimization, Hessian argument and closed-form hyperparameter solutions in Appendix B.5, plus stationary-point analyses of human-proposed laws in A.4. Appendix B.1 also revises the mathematical definitions of NMSE and NMAE.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes automated discovery, exact recovery in two scenarios and improved fitting in others. v2 makes SLDBench a core contribution and claims consistently superior extrapolation to human laws across all seven tasks, effectiveness across multiple LLMs, and demonstrated pretraining and fine-tuning utility. These substantially broaden the claims beyond renaming or stronger adjectives.

C2.justification: The irreducible-loss interpretation already appears in v1. v2 adds an effective-pretraining-data interpretation for SFT and an argument that the human MoE law diverges at large model size. It also interprets iteration trajectories as evidence against overfitting. Dedicated discussions of leakage, passive-data constraints and potentially poor extrapolation of one discovered law disappear; limitations instead emphasize benchmark scope, unexplored datasets and agent specialization.

D1.justification: v2 adds task prompt templates and submission interfaces (Appendix C), baseline package versions (B.6), discovered-law code and fitted coefficients (B.4-B.5), and detailed population, selection, timeout, retry and execution settings (D). These greatly expand documentation beyond v1's shorter setup descriptions. The stated code-access URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands toward coding agents, AI scientists and benchmarks such as SWE-bench, MLE-bench, ScienceAgentBench and PaperBench. v2 substantively contrasts SLDBench's real experimental data and control groups with existing scientific-discovery benchmarks. Parallel-scaling, Step Law and additional agent literature are added, while several earlier symbolic-regression references and their discussion disappear.

P1.justification: The title and method name change, and the abstract, introduction and central narrative are extensively rewritten around a benchmark-first presentation. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, the formal exposition is condensed, and retained human-law formulas move into Appendix A.3. Appendices organize prompts, configurations and supplementary evidence.

P2.justification: The co-evolution diagram is redrawn and becomes Figure 2. The earlier MoE panels and coefficient table are removed; new displays include the agent-performance bar chart, hyperparameter heatmap and iteration curves. Dataset and result tables are redesigned, with separate main-text R2 comparisons and appendix error-metric, uncertainty and ablation tables.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's limited extrapolation coverage and untested practical-utility claims, while adding uncertainty reporting and detailed configurations. However, its stronger superiority claims rely on unreconciled results: CodeX with GPT-5 has lr_and_bsz R2 of 0.269 in Table 3, whereas Table 5 gives NMSE 0.0597, implying R2 of 0.9403 under Appendix B.1. This materially affects the comparison with SLDAgent. The substantial additions and unresolved reliability of central comparisons prevent a confident net judgment of overall quality.
